task.title: Bounded retry lifecycle
task.specification: Config attempts>=1,delay>=1. Start now=0,phase=idle,id=null,attempt=0,due=null. start{id}: while pending/waiting status=busy; otherwise starts a new job attempt=1,phase=pending, emits {id,attempt:1}, status=started. IDs may be reused after terminal states. fail{id,attempt,after>=0}: only matching current pending attempt counts; if attempt>=attempts set phase=failed,due=null; else phase=waiting,due=now+max(delay,after); status=failed or waiting. success{id,attempt}: matching pending attempt sets succeeded,due=null,status=succeeded. cancel: active pending/waiting->cancelled,due=null,status=cancelled, otherwise ignored. advance{dt>=0}: add dt; if waiting and now>=due increment attempt once,phase=pending,due=null,emit current attempt; status=advanced. Every stale/nonmatching response status=ignored. Output {status,phase,id,attempt,due,now,send:[{id,attempt}]}. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}; initial state is null. Only the current event is available; each named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"run"}. Inputs have at most eight single lowercase ASCII-letter identifiers, safe integer quantities and at most 48 events. Return exactly the documented output fields after every event; state representation is unrestricted JSON. All identifiers and numeric fields shown in event forms are present; quantities and all intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. Regimes vary event order and timing: ordinary uses moderate capacity, boundary tests equality/empty cases, adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events, and shift uses smaller capacities or larger costs/delays within the same semantics. Generator regimes: Shift permits one attempt versus ordinary 3, requiring immediate terminal failure; timing still applies to other regimes. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Dendrochronology
matchedCard.relation: Overlapping sequences can be aligned by distinctive patterns spanning several observations. Cross-comparison can reveal missing or extra local observations that a simple position count would treat as elapsed intervals.
assumptions: The sequences share a comparable underlying history.
The overlap contains enough distinguishing structure to support alignment.
matchedCard.boundary: Repeated patterns or insufficient overlap can support several alignments. A single coincident observation does not establish a unique chronological match.
matchedCard.source_fact: NOAA describes crossdating tree-ring patterns from several trees to account for missing or extra rings and align samples from different periods.

shuffledCard.label: Comparator hysteresis
shuffledCard.relation: A state-dependent comparator uses distinct upper and lower transition thresholds. Between them, the existing state is retained. Fluctuations that remain within this interval need not cause repeated switching.
assumptions: The output has a preceding state.
Distinct thresholds are appropriate to the signal range and acceptable response delay.
shuffledCard.boundary: A wider separation can postpone response to a real change. Behavior with two state-dependent thresholds differs from reacting to every crossing of one fixed threshold.
shuffledCard.source_fact: Texas Instruments describes an inverting comparator with upper and lower hysteresis thresholds to reduce unwanted transitions caused by noise or slow-moving signals.

initial.explanation: The conditional rule is: a response changes lifecycle state only when its ID and attempt match the currently pending job; otherwise it is ignored. Waiting retries become pending exactly once when time reaches the deadline. A terminal job may be started again.
initial.mapping: State variables are now, phase, id, attempt, and due. Events map to transitions: start creates attempt 1 unless busy; matching fail waits or fails; matching success succeeds; cancel terminates active work; advance moves time and emits one retry when due.
initial.assumptions: Unknown event types are treated as ignored. Cancel and advance report their specified operational status even when they make no state transition. All supplied values satisfy the stated input constraints.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var s=null;for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){var r=solve({config:input.config,state:s,event:input.events[i]});if(JSON.stringify(r.output)!==JSON.stringify(output[i]))return false;s=r.state}return true}

final.explanation: The lifecycle is tracked with current time, phase, job ID, attempt, and deadline. A start is accepted unless work is pending or waiting. Fail and success affect state only for the matching pending job and attempt. A retry failure enters waiting with a deadline based on the larger of configured delay and the supplied minimum delay. Advance moves time and promotes at most one due retry. Terminal jobs can be started again; irrelevant responses are ignored.

initial.explanation: Apply a single-job state machine: only the current pending attempt accepts responses; waiting retries become pending exactly once when due. Terminal jobs ignore responses and can be restarted.
initial.mapping: config.attempts and delay map to retry limits and waiting deadlines; state tracks now, phase, id, attempt, and due; event responses map to status and optional send.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated schema, safe-integer bounds, and event limits. No event other than the current event is inspected.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||typeof x.status!=="string"||typeof x.phase!=="string"||typeof x.attempt!=="number"||typeof x.now!=="number"||!Array.isArray(x.send))return false;if(!("id"in x)||!("due"in x))return false}return true}

final.explanation: Maintains the single lifecycle state across events. Responses are accepted only for the currently pending matching attempt; waiting retries become pending once their deadline is reached, and terminal jobs may be restarted. Each result contains exactly the required output fields.

initial.explanation: A bounded retry state machine tracks one current job, its attempt, phase, deadline, and logical time. Matching responses mutate only the active pending attempt; stale responses are ignored. Waiting retries activate once when advance reaches the deadline.
initial.mapping: The source rule directly maps config.attempts and config.delay to retry limits and deadlines, state fields to lifecycle state, and event types to transitions and output status.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the published shape and safe-integer bounds. Only the current event and returned JSON state are used.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){var c=input.config,e=input.events,s={n:0,p:'idle',i:null,a:0,d:null},r=[];function o(x){r.push({status:x,phase:s.p,id:s.i,attempt:s.a,due:s.d,now:s.n,send:[]})}for(var z of e){var t=z.type;if(t==='start'){if(s.p==='pending'||s.p==='waiting'){o('busy')}else{s.i=z.id;s.a=1;s.p='pending';s.d=null;o('started');r[r.length-1].send=[{id:s.i,attempt:1}]}}else if(t==='fail'){if(s.p!=='pending'||z.id!==s.i||z.attempt!==s.a)o('ignored');else if(s.a>=c.attempts){s.p='failed';s.d=null;o('failed')}else{s.p='waiting';s.d=s.n+Math.max(c.delay,z.after);o('waiting')}}else if(t==='success'){if(s.p!=='pending'||z.id!==s.i||z.attempt!==s.a)o('ignored');else{s.p='succeeded';s.d=null;o('succeeded')}}else if(t==='cancel'){if(s.p==='pending'||s.p==='waiting'){s.p='cancelled';s.d=null;o('cancelled')}else o('ignored')}else{ s.n+=z.dt;if(s.p==='waiting'&&s.n>=s.d){s.a++;s.p='pending';s.d=null;o('advanced');r[r.length-1].send=[{id:s.i,attempt:s.a}]}else o('advanced')}}return JSON.stringify(r)===JSON.stringify(output)}

final.explanation: A synchronous retry lifecycle state machine stores logical time, current job identity, attempt, phase, and deadline. Starts are rejected while active; matching responses affect only the current pending attempt. Failures either terminate or schedule a deadline using the larger configured delay and requested minimum. Advance updates time and performs at most one eligible retry, emitting its attempt. All outputs include the complete documented snapshot.
